summary: Chi-wah Chan works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1993, studying under Robert Buswell and Benjamin A. Elman, and served as a teaching assistant at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Chia Theng Shen (1913–2007) was a Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions. He also held a post at the Buddhist Association of the United States from circa 1964 to 2007.
Chie Ikeya works in the field of history and archaeology. She completed her PhD at Cornell University in 2006, studying under David K. Wyatt.

Chien Y. Hsu is a Buddhist studies scholar. Hsu studied under doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura (until 2011) and James B. Apple (attested 2013), and under traditional teacher Zhenhua (attested 2013).

Chien-hsing Ho specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Ho served as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from McMaster University under James A. Benn, Nobuyoshi Yamabe, and Canshan Cheng, and became an Assistant Professor at Fo Guang University (attested 2016).

Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) studied religious studies at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University under Bunzaburo Matsumoto. He served as professor at Keijo Imperial University (1927–1941) and Yamaguchi University (1950–1952), alongside posts at Ryukoku, Koyasan, and Hanazono.

Chijun Hamada is a scholar in Buddhist studies. In 1978, Hamada was attested as a research assistant at Taisho University and as a researcher at the university's Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute.

Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's at the University of British Columbia and a PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, Ashok Aklujkar, and Karin Preisendanz, among other teachers.
Chikyo Yamamoto (1913–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1970) and as a part-time lecturer (attested 1980).
Chime Rinpoche (1941–2026) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Gangshar from circa 1956 to 1959 and held a post at the British Library.

Chin Kung (1927–2022) studied under Dongmei Fang, Lee Ping-nan, and the 7th Changkya Khutukhtu. Working in Buddhist studies, religion, and philosophy, he founded the Hwa Dzan Buddhist Library and led the Pure Land Learning College.

Ching Keng works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (circa 2001–2009) under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and became an Associate Professor at National Chengchi University around 2011.

Ching-mei Shyu specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Shyu earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi under Jan Nattier and completed a PhD at Cornell University in 2008 under Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.

Chintaharan Chakravarti (1900–1972) was an Indology scholar. He served as a professor at Presidency University and Presidency College, Chennai, was affiliated with Bethune College (attested 1941), and served as Publication Secretary at Sanskrit Sahitya Parishat (attested 1960).
Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) is an Indologist who founded Silpakorn University and served as its director. He also taught Kazuhiro Yamamoto.

Chisan Koho (1879–1967) studied Buddhist studies at Komazawa University and Kyōdō Kōshūin under several teachers. He held head posts at Saijō-ji and Nagano Ken Senmon Nisodo, served at Soji-ji (circa 1957–1967), and founded Tsurumi University in 1966.
Chisei Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Tanaka held posts at Mampuku-ji Bunkaden, attested in 2003 and attested as director in 2006.
Chisho Namai (born 1945) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Koyasan University, serving as a professor (attested 1996) and as president (attested 2008).

Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) specializes in Indology and philosophy. After earning a master's degree from Kyoto University in 1968, Takenaka was an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1979–1983) and a professor at Tokoha Gakuen University (attested 1989).
